content.content:
Fixture probe. Do exactly this and nothing else — no file reads, no shell, no
other tools. Call AskUserQuestion ONCE with a single question, then stop.

- header: multiSelect
- multiSelect: false
- question: 30 of the 425 asks on disk carry a multiSelect question, where the widget wants space-to-toggle then enter. How should the phone drive that?
- three options, each with a description of three or four full sentences:
  1. label: One tap = one toggle, then a separate done (Recommended)
     description: Tapping an option sends 'step to it + space' and nothing else. The next poll re-reads the pane, which paints the toggle state per row, so the phone renders checked options as checked from the screen rather than from local memory. A separate 'done' button sends enter. Costs a 4s poll per toggle.
  2. label: Collect locally, send one sequence
     description: The phone tracks which options you ticked and, on 'done', sends the whole script: step, space, step, space, enter. One round trip and no poll latency between taps, which matters when you are ticking three of four options. But it is an intermediate state that is never re-read, so one dropped keystroke silently mis-toggles everything after it.
  3. label: Send multiSelect to free text
     description: Render the options read-only and answer through the widget's free-text row in prose. No toggle arithmetic at all, and multiSelect stops being a distinct code path. But it converts a structured answer into text the receiving Claude has to re-interpret, and 30 of 425 is frequent enough that this would be a visible downgrade rather than an edge case.
